problem_type: A paid asynchronous submission is judged by its first response, so "accepted but not finished" is reported as failure
symptom: nomi_try_model against an asynchronous provider returned provider_failed (status=queued, no assets) after the provider had already accepted and charged the job; the AI followed the nextAction, fixed the card and tried again, submitting and charging a second job.
direct_cause: tryModel.ts judged the first runTask result only: succeeded && assets.length > 0, else provider_failed. Asynchronous providers return queued with no assets on first response, and tryModel had no access to the task query chain.
class_root: After-submit waiting had no shared boundary: tryModel judged the first response only. A caller that submits a paid job without a single wait boundary can turn "still running" into "failed" (and the failure text invites a charged retry).
affected_population: Every user whose AI connects an asynchronous image or video provider (most video providers) and runs nomi_try_model
The first sample card in the onboarding kit (asynchronous)
internal_only_reason: The invariant is internal: how Nomi reports the state of a job it has already submitted. No third-party document decides it.
invariants: A non-terminal task status after a successful submit is never reported as provider_failed.
Waiting after submit in tryModel uses pollTaskToTerminal and never re-submits; the wait is capped at 40 seconds (tool-call timeout of external hosts).
When the wait budget runs out, the caller says submitted / still processing, includes the task id, and tells the AI not to retry.

door_reduction.why_not: Each door is a distinct role: tryModel judges the result; pollTaskToTerminal is the single wait; dispatcher.ts and dispatch.ts only pass dependencies down; envelope.ts defines the result shape; onboardingVerbs.ts is the AI-facing text. None duplicates another.

generality_proof: tryModel is the only caller of pollTaskToTerminal, which only returns a terminal result or an explicit ended=timeout/poll_failed and never invents a failure. tryModel maps non-terminal outcomes to still_processing, so no provider, task kind or status vocabulary can reach provider_failed unless the provider itself reported a terminal failure. The generateOnProject family is deleted by the convergence step 0 and will then leave this as the single wait.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: The only after-submit wait: polls the shared fetchTaskResult chain, retries query errors for free, never re-submits, reports the end reason instead of fabricating a failure.
Maps wait outcomes to results: succeeded with assets, provider_failed only on a terminal failure, still_processing otherwise.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: No code path from a non-terminal status to provider_failed; waits through pollTaskToTerminal capped at 40s.
Already polls inline; the whole family is deleted by the convergence step 0, so it is deliberately not touched here.

ComfyUI certification already loops while status is queued or running with its own 300s abort; it never judges the first response. It is a third poller and is listed in residual_risks, not changed here.
The first-frame helper has its own short poll loop that gives up silently because the frame is an optional gain; it never reports failure of a paid job to the AI.

recurrence.reason: Any new caller that submits a paid job through runTask can repeat the first-response judgement; the AI-facing text also invited a retry.
same_class_scan: node scripts/door-map.mjs tryModel (2 doors) and fetchTaskResult (13 doors)
grep for runTask callers: generateOnProject polls; comfyCandidateTest polls; productionRunService polls through its own run state; credentialProbeConfirm has no paid submit

prevention.invariant: A submitted job's non-terminal state is never reported as a failure.
prevention.failure_mode: Wait budget exhausted or query chain down: return still_processing with the task id and an explicit do-not-retry instruction.
prevention.strategy: One wait function owned by the capability core; both callers import it. tryModel has no code path from a non-terminal status to provider_failed.

legacy_paths.rationale: The old first-response-only judgement in tryModel was replaced in place; generateOnProject's own loop is removed by the convergence step 0, not here.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party runtime controls the invariant.

migration: No stored data changes. A new still_processing code is added to the onboarding failure envelope; older AI clients treat unknown ok:false codes as not-ok and read nextAction, which says not to retry.
residual_risks: Task lookup by id for the AI (a nomi_read target) is a follow-up, suggested for 0.24 B line.
The AI has no tool to look a task up by id; it can only tell the user the task id. A later "look up this task" read target is not part of this hot fix.
ComfyUI certification and renderStaticFrame keep their own poll loops (third and second copies); folding them into pollTaskToTerminal is a separate change.
Closing the window or quitting Nomi during the wait loses the in-process task cache; the provider job and its charge continue (see the design card mid-way table).

invariant_owner_layer.why: The single after-submit wait never invents a failure for a job the provider has accepted; tryModel maps its end reason to still_processing.
